articles.title: High-Speed Boat Crash Near Dhari Devi Temple Triggers Nationwide Safety Debate
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: On February 15, 2026, a viral video showing a high-speed collision between two motorboats on the Alaknanda River near the revered Dhari Devi Temple in Uttarakhand’s Pauri district sparked a nationwide debate over river safety and adventure tourism protocols.

body.html:
On February 15, 2026, a viral video showing a high-speed collision between two motorboats on the Alaknanda River near the revered Dhari Devi Temple in Uttarakhand’s Pauri district sparked a nationwide debate over river safety and adventure tourism protocols.

The footage shows two motorboats travelling in the same direction when the front vessel suddenly veers left into the path of a trailing boat attempting to overtake at speed. Within seconds, the boats collide forcefully.

The impact caused one boat to spin uncontrollably and reportedly threw a boat operator into the river. According to reports, the operator jumped into the water moments before the crash to save himself and was later rescued by nearby locals.

Fortunately, no passengers were on board at the time of the incident. No injuries or fatalities have been reported.

The near-miss has reignited concerns over river navigation and adventure sports safety in the region:

Coordination Gaps: Preliminary inputs suggest lack of coordination between boat operators and strong river currents may have contributed to the accident.

Safety Protocols Under Review: Authorities are reviewing existing safety standards amid public demands for stricter regulations, mandatory certified training for operators and regular equipment audits.

Sensitive Location: The Dhari Devi Temple is a high-footfall pilgrimage site. Experts warn that such incidents pose significant risks to tourists and could impact the religious sanctity of the area.

The incident has intensified calls for tighter oversight of commercial boating activities on the Alaknanda River, particularly in high-traffic religious zones.

articles.title: Lucknow Era Hospital Violence: 30 Guards Attack Advocate Adarsh Singh over Parking
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A shocking incident of violence has come to light from Era Hospital in the Thakurganj area, where around 30 bouncers and guards of a private hospital allegedly assaulted a lawyer and his two friends over a parking dispute on the night of February 19.

body.html:
Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A shocking incident of violence has come to light from Era Hospital in the Thakurganj area, where around 30 bouncers and guards of a private hospital allegedly assaulted a lawyer and his two friends over a parking dispute on the night of February 19.

According to reports, Advocate Adarsh Singh, a resident of New Haiderganj, had gone to the hospital to visit the ailing mother of his friend Shubham Yadav, who is admitted there. Shubham Yadav and another friend, Pradeep Yadav, accompanied him. The trio had parked their Scorpio vehicle near the hospital gate when guards objected, leading to a verbal argument.

The minor dispute allegedly escalated into violence after heated exchanges. It is claimed that around 30 guards arrived at the spot armed with sticks and iron rods and began brutally assaulting the three men. When they tried to flee, the guards reportedly chased them, knocked them to the ground and continued beating them.

Advocate Adarsh Singh sustained a severe head injury and required multiple stitches. His two friends were also injured in the attack. The lawyer has alleged that ₹10,000 was looted during the assault. All three were admitted for medical treatment.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the hospital premises. The footage reportedly shows the argument over parking, followed by several guards rushing out with sticks and rods and attacking the victims. In one clip, police personnel can be seen taking some guards into custody.

On receiving information, local police reached the spot and detained several guards for questioning. CCTV footage has been examined and nearby persons were also questioned.

Thakurganj Inspector Omvir Singh Chauhan said the dispute arose over vehicle parking. A complaint has been received from the advocate’s side, and legal action is being initiated after investigation.

#Lucknow #UttarPradesh #HospitalViolence #ParkingDispute #LawyerAssaulted #CCTVFootage #Thakurganj #BreakingNews

body.html:
Deoria (Salempur): An attempt to rob a jeweller at gunpoint in broad daylight created panic in the busy Kishoreganj market area under Kotwali police station limits on Thursday.

According to police, Dhruv Kumar Verma, a resident of Ward No. 10, Kishoreganj, runs a jewellery shop on Sant Tulsi Marg. At around 11:05 am, an unidentified person entered the shop with his face covered with a cloth. The accused allegedly pointed a firearm at Verma and attempted to loot the shop.

Acting swiftly, the jeweller locked himself inside the strong room, forcing the miscreant to flee the spot empty-handed. The incident triggered fear among nearby traders and locals.

Verma has demanded registration of an FIR against the unknown accused. Kotwali in-charge Inspector Mahendra Kumar Chaturvedi reached the spot and carried out an inspection. Police said further investigation is underway.

articles.title: TV Volume Dispute Turns Deadly: AC Mechanic Stabbed by Wife in Mangalagiri
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 27-year-old AC mechanic was allegedly stabbed to death by his wife following a heated argument at their residence in a TIDCO housing complex in Mangalagiri.

body.html:
A 27-year-old AC mechanic was allegedly stabbed to death by his wife following a heated argument at their residence in a TIDCO housing complex in Mangalagiri.

The deceased, Sheikh Ahmed, reportedly asked his wife to lower the television volume, which led to a verbal altercation that quickly escalated. In a fit of rage, the woman allegedly attacked him with a knife.

Neighbours rushed Ahmed to the Government General Hospital in Vijayawada, where he succumbed to his injuries during treatment.

Police said the accused has been taken into custody. A case has been registered and further investigation is underway to ascertain the exact sequence of events.

Earlier this month, a similar incident was reported from Rangareddy district, where a man allegedly stabbed his ex-wife to death at an apartment in Green City Colony. Police said the woman had divorced the accused and remarried, which reportedly triggered the attack.

Vanasthalipuram Police reached the spot and initiated an investigation. “We received information about the matter, reached the spot and are investigating the matter,” a police official said.

Further details are awaited.

articles.title: Sloganeering During Shiv Jayanti Procession Sparks Brief Tension in Amberpet
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension prevailed in Amberpet on Thursday night, February 19, after participants in a procession marking Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti allegedly raised slogans in front of Jamia Masjid Amberpet during Taraweeh prayers.

body.html:
Tension prevailed in Amberpet on Thursday night, February 19, after participants in a procession marking Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti allegedly raised slogans in front of Jamia Masjid Amberpet during Taraweeh prayers.

The incident occurred around 10 pm as the procession passed the mosque. According to local reports, slogans were raised while prayers were underway. Some worshippers returning from the mosque gathered outside and reportedly responded with counter-slogans. The exchange lasted for nearly five minutes before police personnel stationed in the area intervened and dispersed both groups.

Additional forces were deployed as a precautionary measure. Rakshita Murthy, DCP of the Secunderabad zone, reached the spot, interacted with community elders, and appealed for calm. She stated that the situation arose after a few individuals raised slogans and confirmed that an enquiry is underway.

Police officials said the situation is currently peaceful and urged residents not to pay heed to rumours.

articles.title: Spa Raid Turns Into ₹40,000 ‘Extortion’ Row in Bareilly? Hindu Outfit Members Under Scanner
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: An alleged extortion attempt has surfaced in the Baradari police station area of Bareilly after action was taken against a spa centre on Pilibhit Road.

body.html:
An alleged extortion attempt has surfaced in the Baradari police station area of Bareilly after action was taken against a spa centre on Pilibhit Road.

According to reports, individuals linked to the Hindu Jagran Manch conducted a sting operation at the spa, alleging prostitution was being carried out under the guise of wellness services. Videos of the alleged activities were recorded and circulated on social media.

Following this, police raided the premises and seized one spa centre.

The matter escalated after allegations emerged that ₹40,000 was demanded from the spa operator in exchange for deleting the videos and helping reopen the centre. Ashu Yadav has been accused of seeking money, allegedly invoking the name of Rishabh Thakur, said to be a district-level leader of a Hindu organisation.

Sources claim the demand was made to settle the issue and prevent further action. The authenticity of the extortion allegations and the role of those involved are under scrutiny.

Police have not issued any official statement so far. The matter is reportedly under investigation.

articles.title: Missing 20-Year-Old Found: The Truth Behind Himanshi and Rahul Yadav’s Marriage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 20-year-old woman who went missing from Lalitpur on February 13, 2026, has surfaced in a viral video claiming she married her partner of her own free will and accusing her family and police of harassment.

body.html:
A 20-year-old woman who went missing from Lalitpur on February 13, 2026, has surfaced in a viral video claiming she married her partner of her own free will and accusing her family and police of harassment.

The woman, identifying herself as Himanshi, said she married Rahul Yadav voluntarily. “I am 20 years old. I got married of my own free will. If anything happens to me, my family, the police and my relatives will be responsible,” she said in the video. She also alleged that police were threatening her in-laws with false cases and harassing her pregnant mother-in-law and her husband’s friends.

The incident falls under the Kotwali Sadar police station limits. According to police, the woman went missing from her home around 9 pm on February 13. Her father lodged a missing person complaint at Kotwali police station, following which a case was registered and a search operation initiated.

The video surfaced on February 18 and has since circulated widely on social media. In the clip, the woman further alleged harassment by the police and warned if she and her husband were troubled.

In a statement, Lalitpur Police said that a case has been registered under relevant sections based on the complaint and that investigation is underway. The Circle Officer (Sadar) has been directed to probe the allegations and take necessary action.

Police said further action will depend on the findings of the ongoing inquiry.

articles.title: Woman Constable Accuses SHO of Misconduct in Basti, Probe Ordered
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman constable posted at Sadar police station in Basti has accused the station house officer (SHO) of making obscene remarks, denying leave, and threatening to assault her.

body.html:
A woman constable posted at Sadar police station in Basti has accused the station house officer (SHO) of making obscene remarks, denying leave, and threatening to assault her.

Constable Maneka Chauhan, a 2019-batch officer from Barhalganj in Gorakhpur, alleged that she had sought a day’s earned leave to visit her ailing mother, who is admitted to Durgavati Hospital. “When I requested leave, he misbehaved with me, abused me and even tried to beat me,” she said, breaking down while speaking to senior officers.

She further alleged that the SHO, Inspector Dinesh Chandra Chaudhary, made inappropriate comments, asked her to call him “brother-in-law,” and insisted she contact him on his personal number. “I refused. He got angry and started harassing me. He marked me absent when I went to duty,” she claimed.

Chauhan, accompanied by her five-year-old daughter, approached Sanjeev Tyagi to lodge a complaint. She also alleged she was stopped from meeting the Superintendent of Police and that the SHO sent a subordinate to monitor her movements.

The constable claimed that several other women personnel had faced similar behaviour but remained silent out of fear of suspension or transfer. She alleged the harassment had pushed her towards suicidal thoughts, but her husband—also a constable posted at Old Basti police station—intervened.

Inspector Chaudhary has denied the allegations, terming them baseless. He said the constable had sought 40–45 days’ leave, which could not be granted due to ongoing examinations, Holi deployment and shortage of force. “We offered 20 days’ leave, but she insisted on 45 days. After that, she made these allegations,” he said.

Additional Superintendent of Police Shyamkant confirmed that a two-member inquiry committee, comprising himself and CO Harraiya Swarnim Singh, has been constituted on the directions of the SP. The committee will submit its report after investigation, and appropriate action will follow.

The matter remains under inquiry.
